sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Dual Control System**: The Act created a **Board of Control** to supervise the Company's political affairs, while the **Court of Directors** retained control over commercial affairs.
• **Subordination**: The Governor-General of Bengal was given more power, and the Presidencies of Bombay and Madras were made strictly subordinate to the Governor-General in matters of war, diplomacy, and revenue.
• **British Possessions**: For the first time, the Company's territories in India were officially termed as **'British Possessions in India'**.
• **Key Metric**: The Act reduced the strength of the Governor-General's Council from four members to three, ensuring the Governor-General could exercise a casting vote.

A committee of three directors from the Court of Directors through which the Board of Control channeled its secret orders to India.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Centralization**: Strengthened the Governor-General's authority over the Presidencies.
• **Accountability**: Introduced the requirement for Company officials to disclose their assets upon returning to Britain.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: The 'Dual Control' led to administrative friction between the Board of Control and the Court of Directors.
• **Solutions**: Eventually led to the total abolition of the Company's administrative powers in the 1858 Act.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'B-C-D' (Board, Control, Dual).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Board of Control created, Dual government established.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Board of Control' (created by Pitts India Act) with the 'Court of Directors' (existing since the Company's inception). Remember: Board = Political/Crown; Court = Commercial/Company.
Mains Value Addition: Use the phrase 'The Act of 1784 was the first step towards the establishment of a formal British Raj by subordinating the Company to the British Cabinet'.

keyTakeaways: Established the system of Dual Government (Diarchy) in India.
Distinguished clearly between the political and commercial functions of the Company.
Asserted the British government's supreme control over the Company's administration.
